Two Russian men have been found guilty by an Angolan court of terrorism and spying after being accused of planning a coup and helping to organise deadly demonstrations in the southern African country last year.

guardian.description:
September exercise called off after Kenya raises concerns over funding and jurisdiction for criminal offences

The British army has been forced to cancel training for its troops in Kenya after the Kenyan government refused to ratify a bilateral defence agreement.

While the UK government wanted to renew the existing agreement, Kenyan lawmakers had sought changes to give local authorities greater powers to hold British soldiers accountable for any offences committed in the country.</

guardian.description:
UK resident was evacuated from Democratic Republic of the Congo where there is an outbreak of the disease

A humanitarian worker is being monitored at a specialist hospital in London after potential exposure to the Ebola virus.

The UK resident was medically evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) where the worker had been treating patients with the disease, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said.

Global hunger declined for the third year in a row in 2025 but experts call for action to bring down costs of fruit, vegetables and dairy as report shows 2.69bn people can’t afford to eat well

One in three people cannot afford to eat a healthy diet, a new report has found, prompting calls for urgent action on food affordability.

Valentín Lavín Romero is the 14th mayor to be murdered since Claudia Sheinbaum became president in 2024

guardian.description:
US secretary of state says international community should ‘join forces’ against authoritarian Ortega regime

guardian.description:
Researchers listening off the Caribbean island of Dominica found variations in the mammals’ audible clicks when marine traffic was close

guardian.description:
Dunedin will be the focal point, having last experienced such an eclipse in 1163 – before any humans reached New Zealand

guardian.description:
Isabel Rose, 26, sentenced to six years for blackmail and perverting course of public justice over her allegations against British man

A British woman who reported being raped to police in Hong Kong has been sentenced to six years in prison for blackmail and perverting the course of public justice.

Isabel Rose, 26, from south-east London, travelled to Hong Kong in early 2024 to visit a British banker she had met while travelling in south-east Asia.

rfi.title: Macky Sall pledges to restore trust in UN as leadership race gathers pace
rfi.description: Former Senegalese president Macky Sall has pledged to restore trust in the United Nations and make the organisation more responsive, as he seeks to become the first African to lead the global body in almost three decades.

rfi.title: European Union slams 'inflammatory' Houthi Red Sea tanker attack
rfi.description: The European Union's top diplomat demanded on Thursday that the Houthis cease attacks on ships in the Red Sea, after a Saudi vessel was hit by the Iran-backed rebels.

rfi.title: Ghanaians ask ICC to investigate xenophobic violence in South Africa
rfi.description: Two Ghanaian nationals have petitioned the International Criminal Court to open a preliminary investigation into attacks on foreign nationals in South Africa, arguing the violence could amount to crimes against humanity, as Ghana's president repeated his call on Thursday for the African Union to address the ongoing unrest.

rfi.title: Wildfire sees 12,000 residents and tourists evacuated in south-west France
rfi.description: A wildfire near Bordeaux in south-west France has led to the evacuation of a further 7,000 people on Thursday, bringing the total number of tourists and residents moved to 12,000, local authorities said.

rfi.title: Germany approves factory use for controversial French-Russian nuclear project
rfi.description: German authorities on Wednesday gave the green light to a controversial French-Russian nuclear project which will use a factory based in Germany for production, and which critics fear will enable spying and sabotage by Moscow.

rfi.title: Zizou's back: Zinedine Zidane set to take charge of Les Bleus
rfi.description: The French Football Federation will hold a news conference on 28 July to unveil the next coach of the national team, the governing body said on Thursday. Former star player Zinedine Zidane has long been viewed as the leading candidate for the role.

rfi.title: DRC's Ebola outbreak kills more than 1,000, with children hit hardest
rfi.description: More than 1,030 people have died from an Ebola outbreak declared in May in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda, the World Health Organization said on Wednesday, as confirmed cases in the DRC surpassed 2,530, according to government data.

rfi.title: United States announces landmark civilian nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia
rfi.description: The United States on Wednesday announced a deal with Saudi Arabia that would establish a civilian nuclear programme in the Gulf country, with Washington insisting the agreement includes nonproliferation safeguards.

rfi.title: Macron talks environment minister out of quitting over pesticide U-turn
rfi.description: France's environment minister, Monique Barbut, will remain in her post, given the "urgency" to act on climate change, after submitting her resignation to President Emmanuel Macron over a bill to reintroduce bee-harming pesticides, her team said Wednesday.

rfi.title: French model recruiter with links to Epstein found dead near Paris
rfi.description: French modelling scout Daniel Siad, 69, who had close ties to convicted American sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, has been found dead at his home outside Paris, prosecutors and his lawyer have said.

rfi.title: France approves social media ban for children under 15, in EU first
rfi.description: French lawmakers have approved a ban on social media access for children under the age of 15, as concerns grow globally over the impact such platforms have on the health and safety of minors.

rfi.title: Gabon and France deepen industrial cooperation with Eramet manganese deal
rfi.description: French mining group Eramet is considering a major expansion of manganese processing in Gabon under an agreement that could strengthen the country’s industrial base, modernise its railway network and reduce its reliance on exports of unprocessed ore.

rfi.title: Germany looks to Azerbaijan as Armenia ties shift regional relationships
rfi.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev have signed a series of economic agreements aimed at deepening Berlin's access to Baku's gas reserves and transit routes. The deal comes as Germany works to diversify its energy supply, and as Azerbaijan balances a Europe-leaning Armenia against a recently repaired relationship with Moscow.

rfi.title: France’s emergency agriculture bill passed, amid divisions over pesticides
rfi.description: France’s National Assembly has approved an emergency agriculture bill after a tense overnight debate, clearing the way for the possible temporary return of two pesticides banned in the country but still authorised elsewhere in the European Union.

rfi.title: France and Germany move to tackle EU’s growing trade deficit with China
rfi.description: France and Germany are pressing for a stronger European Union response to China’s growing trade surplus and industrial overcapacity, as concerns mount over the impact on key European sectors.

rfi.title: Ukraine’s wartime unity put to the test by protests over military leadership
rfi.description: Protests over the dismissal of Ukraine’s reformist defence minister entered a fifth day on Monday, deepening a political crisis that has placed President Volodymyr Zelensky under mounting pressure to overhaul the country’s military leadership.

rfi.title: Countdown to the ballot: Zambia gears up for August elections
rfi.description: This week on Spotlight on Africa, we're heading to Zambia, where general elections are set to take place on the 13th August. Voters will go to the polls to elect a president, members of the National Assembly, councillors and council chairs. Incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema has already picked up endorsements from within his own camp, the UPND Alliance, the coalition that's held power since 2021. So what's at stake, and who's in the running?

rfi.title: Senegal's Faye backs former president Sall's bid for UN top job in U-turn
rfi.description: Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye has endorsed former president Macky Sall's candidacy to become the next United Nations secretary-general, the foreign ministry said on Monday, giving his predecessor crucial backing from his home country despite deep political divisions.

euronews.title: Divorces in Spain fall 2.7% in 2025 as shared custody becomes the norm
euronews.description: Spain recorded 83,683 marital break-ups in 2025, 2.7% fewer than a year earlier. Shared custody of children has now overtaken sole custody awarded to mothers.

euronews.title: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announces cabinet overhaul
euronews.description: Nina Warken is set to succeed Thorsten Frei (CDU) as head of the chancellery. Carsten Linnemann, who had been serving as the general secretary of Merz's CDU party, is then to take over Warken's role as health minister.

euronews.title: Ukrainian drone strike ignites major blaze at Saint Petersburg warehouses
euronews.description: A Ukrainian drone strike sparked a major fire at a Wildberries warehouse near Saint Petersburg early on Thursday 24 July, sending thick smoke across the city and temporarily disrupting flights at Pulkovo Airport, according to Russian authorities.

euronews.title: Ireland finds 'no evidence' to conclude alumina sales prop up Russia's war
euronews.description: The long-awaited investigation into Ireland's alumina exports to Russia has concluded on an ambivalent note, with the government neither fullying confirming nor denying any link to Vladimir Putin's war machine.

euronews.title: 9 in 10 Europeans would consider moving abroad – here's where they would go
euronews.description: After polling 2,000 adults across France, Germany, Italy and the UK, Spain emerged as the top choice for would-be expats considering starting a new life in a different country.

euronews.title: France: Massive blaze engulfs Cap Ferret forests as thousands evacuated
euronews.description: A fast-moving wildfire forced the evacuation of the entire Cap Ferret peninsula after destroying dozens of homes, as 700 firefighters battled to contain the blaze.

euronews.title: Southern Europe still battling wildfires as Spain declares national emergency in Madrid region
euronews.description: Spain has declared a national emergency as wildfires threaten the Madrid region, while France seeks EU help and Italy battles blazes across Sicily.

euronews.title: 'Expect more action from the US after the Google fine,' top EU lawmaker says
euronews.description: German Socialist MEP Bernd Lange, the European Parliament's trade chief, told Euronews that he hopes the new US tariffs will be challenged in US courts and said that targeting the EU over forced labour was "crazy" given its stringent regulations.

euronews.title: EU’s €1bn-a-day trade gap with China an 'unsustainable reality', says EU Parliament VP
euronews.description: Javi López, European Parliament vice-president, says the European Union's trade imbalance with China "cannot continue", with the bloc running a €1bn-a-day trade deficit.

euronews.title: The EU is walking a tightrope between the world's major hegemons
euronews.description: In today's newsletter: Trump announces tariff threats from across the transatlantic, while Euronews speaks with an MEP fresh off a trip to China, and analysis on what happened with the EU's 21st sanctions package against Russia.

euronews.title: Short breaks set the tone for travellers in Greece, new data reveals
euronews.description: Data from the Hellenic Statistical Authority show that trips of up to three nights recorded the strongest growth in 2025. Citizens over 65 emerged as the age group with the sharpest increase in travel.

euronews.title: Raging gods and treacherous odysseys: Take our quiz to test your knowledge about Greek mythology
euronews.description: As Christopher Nolan's adaptation of Homer's "The Odyssey" continues its god-like reign over the box office, Euronews Culture tests your knowledge of Greek mythology.

euronews.title: Spain coach slams Argentina's World Cup final behaviour as 'unacceptable’
euronews.description: Argentina's antics following the final whistle in the World Cup final have prompted FIFA to launch a disciplinary investigation.

euronews.title: The majority of AI jobs now sit outside technological occupations in Europe
euronews.description: AI-labelled job titles in postings have been increasing rapidly across Europe. However, these opportunities are no longer limited to AI or data jobs as most are now in non-tech positions.

euronews.title: ‘Less than a minute of your time’: Driving the speed limit could save you money and cut emissions
euronews.description: A new study says that obeying the speed limit could save millions of euros every year, while adding just 54 seconds to the average daily commute.

euronews.title: ‘Like a bird flying’: You can now soar on a giant swing over the Swiss Alps
euronews.description: The 12m-high swing opened earlier this month and hopes to attract off-season visitors as snow becomes less reliable due to climate change.

euronews.title: Europe Today: Trump imposes new tariffs as EU agrees fresh sanctions on Russia
euronews.description: US President Donald Trump is imposing a new wave of tariffs on trading partners, including the EU, with levies ranging between 10 and 12.5%. Bernd Lange, the EU Parliament top lawmaker on trade, reacts to this measure. Also in Brussels: The EU has agreed a new round of sanctions against Russia.

euronews.title: Why the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history is becoming more challenging
euronews.description: The fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history has killed more than 1,000 people in eastern Congo as health officials race to contain the virus amid ongoing conflict, mistrust and the absence of an approved treatment.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, incendies : la préfecture ordonne l’évacuation « de l’ensemble de la presqu’île » du cap Ferret, le feu a parcouru plus de 10 000 hectares
lemonde.description: La préfecture a ordonné ce matin « l’évacuation progressive de l’ensemble de la presqu’île du Bassin d’Arcachon, village après village, de Claouey jusqu’à la pointe du cap Ferret ». Aucun nouveau blessé n’est à déplorer à ce stade, précise-t-elle.

lemonde.title: Concert interrompu de Barbara Butch : pour « l’insoumis » Bally Bagayoko, la DJ « a raison » de porter plainte
lemonde.description: Samedi soir, à Grenoble, le concert de l’artiste, de confession juive, avait été interrompu au bout d’une vingtaine de minutes en raison d’une action de militants propalestiniens et de LFI. Ils répondaient à un appel au boycott lancé notamment par la section iséroise des « insoumis ».

lemonde.title: Posez vos questions sur l’interdiction des réseaux sociaux aux moins de 15 ans
lemonde.description: Députés et sénateurs ont adopté, mardi 21 juillet, l’interdiction des réseaux sociaux aux moins de 15 ans. Florian Reynaud et Morgane Tual, journalistes au service Pixels du « Monde », répondent à vos questions par tchat à partir de 10 heures.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : une attaque de drones ukrainiens à Saint-Pétersbourg provoque un incendie dans un entrepôt
lemonde.description: « La frappe a visé des installations d’infrastructures civiles », a déclaré le gouverneur de la ville, Alexandre Beglov. Selon des images diffusées sur les réseaux sociaux et des médias locaux, des entrepôts appartenant au géant du commerce en ligne Wildberries, l’équivalent russe d’Amazon, ont été ciblés.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : en Bretagne, Gabriel Attal mène campagne pour faire décoller sa candidature
lemonde.description: Arpentant trois jours la région, le candidat à l’Elysée s’est affiché, jeudi, aux côtés du patron Michel-Edouard Leclerc et a martelé sa volonté de réduire « l’écart entre le [salaire] net et le brut ». La trêve estivale est l’occasion pour lui de multiplier les déplacements pour se maintenir dans la course.

lemonde.title: En Inde, le gouvernement peine à désamorcer un mouvement de contestation qui cible désormais Narendra Modi
lemonde.description: Après avoir tenté d’ignorer la mobilisation étudiante des « cafards » dénonçant  la corruption du système éducatif, le premier ministre, Narendra Modi, se voit de plus en plus mis en cause, alors que les partis d’opposition et plusieurs personnalités du cinéma populaire Bollywood ont apporté leur soutien au mouvement.

lemonde.title: Les Etats membres de la CPI s’apprêtent à décider du sort de son procureur, suspendu pour un « usage abusif de pouvoir ou d’autorité » sur son assistante
lemonde.description: Dans un contexte d’attaques américaines contre la Cour pénale internationale, les Etats membres de la juridiction votent, vendredi 24 juillet, pour ou contre la révocation de Karim Khan.

lemonde.title: Donald Trump ne s’opposera pas à l’extradition des frères Tate vers le Royaume-Uni, selon la Maison Blanche
lemonde.description: « Il n’y a aucun rôle à jouer pour nous à ce stade, et peut-être même jamais, dans cette affaire », a déclaré mercredi le secrétaire d’Etat américain, Marco Rubio.

lemonde.title: Quatre bassines d’irrigation doivent être démantelées en Charente-Maritime, ordonne la justice
lemonde.description: Selon l’association à l’origine du contentieux, de nombreux manquements ont entaché l’édification de ces réserves d’eau. Les agriculteurs ont décidé de faire appel de cette décision qui leur donne trois ans pour remettre les lieux en état.

lemonde.title: L’été au bureau vu par Colcanopa : business plantes
lemonde.description: « L’été au bureau » (2/7). Le dessinateur Colcanopa a imaginé pour La Matinale du « Monde » les pérégrinations récréatives, et tout aussi loufoques, de salariés pendant les congés de leurs collègues. Et si finalement, rester au bureau pendant l’été, c’était déjà partir un peu ?

lemonde.title: Dans « Les Perméables », Judith Vanistendael se tient au chevet des migrants belges de 2071
lemonde.description: « Une planche de BD de la rentrée » (2/5). L’autrice imagine des réfugiés climatiques européens confrontés aux règles kafkaïennes de leur société d’accueil, sur les îles Lofoten, en Norvège.

lemonde.title: En Chine, la célébration opportune des Tigres volants américains
lemonde.description: Cet escadron, qui a appuyé l’armée chinoise dans les airs contre les avancées japonaises durant la seconde guerre mondiale, est exploité diplomatiquement par Pékin pour essayer d’influer sur l’attitude de Washington à son égard.

lemonde.title: Chez Jars, dans la Drôme : du grès émaillé top secret
lemonde.description: « Tour de France de savoir-faire d’exception » (2/5). Fondé en 1857 dans le village d’Anneyron, l’atelier Jars propose de la vaisselle artisanale en grès, dont la recette est jalousement gardée. L’application d’émaux offre une vaste palette de couleurs à ces assiettes, tasses et bols.

france24fr.title: En Cisjordanie occupée, un Israélien et quatre Palestiniens tués dans des violences
france24fr.description: Un Israélien et quatre Palestiniens ont été tués vendredi dans des violences dans le nord de la Cisjordanie occupée. Le Premier ministre israélien Benjamin Netanyahu a assuré que son gouvernement agirait "avec fermeté contre les terroristes et leurs commanditaires".

france24fr.title: L'Espagne toujours en proie aux flammes, l'état d'urgence décrété près de Madrid
france24fr.description: Les violents incendies près de Madrid et dans la province d'Avila restent hors de contrôle vendredi, aggravés par une météo défavorable. Le gouvernement espagnol a décrété la veille "l'état d'urgence d'intérêt national" près de la capitale, un dispositif qui permet de mobiliser plus de ressources pour éteindre les feux.

france24fr.title: Nouvelle-Calédonie, la fracture
france24fr.description: Depuis des décennies, la Nouvelle-Calédonie est un territoire fracturé entre indépendantiste et loyalistes. france24fr.title: Incendie en Gironde : la préfecture ordonne d'évacuer l'ensemble de la presqu'île du Cap-Ferret

france24fr.title: Huit des 12 dauphins du Marineland d'Antibes ont été transférés en Espagne
france24fr.description: Huit des 12 dauphins restants au Marineland d'Antibes, fermé depuis janvier 2025, ont été transférés jeudi dans un parc à Benalmadena, près de Malaga, en Espagne. Ces cétacés pourraient revenir plus tard en France dans un centre d'accueil en projet au zoo de Beauval.

france24fr.title: Les six candidats à la succession d'Antonio Guterres débattent sur l'avenir de l'ONU
france24fr.description: La Chilienne Michelle Bachelet, l'Équatorienne Maria Fernanda Espinosa, l'Argentin Rafael Grossi, la Costaricaine Rebeca Grynspan, la Guyanienne Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett et le Sénégalais Macky Sall, tous candidats à la succession d'Antonio Guterres à la tête de l'ONU, ont débattu jeudi soir pendant deux heures, sans jamais s'interpeller directement.

france24fr.title: Les États-Unis imposent de nouveaux droits de douane à une soixantaine de pays

france24fr.title: Ebola en RDC et en Ouganda : le bilan dépasse désormais les 1 000 morts, selon l'OMS

france24fr.title: Ghana : pourquoi les accusations de sorcellerie continuent-elles de tuer ?

france24fr.title: Au Maroc, les soutiens du rappeur Mehdi Black Wind réclament sa libération
france24fr.description: Au Maroc, le rappeur Mehdi Black Wind est en détention provisoire depuis le 13 juillet. Connu pour ses textes critiques sur les inégalités marocaines, il a été arrêté à l'aéroport de Rabat alors qu'il s'apprêtait à rejoindre la France où il réside. france24fr.title: L'épidémie d'Ebola a déjà fait plus de 1000 morts en RDC et en Ouganda

nzz.title: Eine radikale Idee sorgt für Kontroversen: In Basel soll die Innenstadt sogar vom öffentlichen Verkehr befreit werden

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Zunehmende Hitzewellen: Europas Klimapolitik braucht mehr Anpassung, weniger Illusionen

nzz.title: Preishoch bei Benzin und Diesel: Autolenker haben noch mehr Probleme als den Iran-Krieg

phys-org.title: Young rift flanks suggest Venus remains tectonically active
phys-org.description: Venus is an inhospitable place, with temperatures soaring to several hundred degrees Celsius (hundreds of degrees Fahrenheit) and no oceans like those on Earth. Planetary scientists long believed Venus was geologically dormant. However, recent research indicates that Venus remains geologically "alive" and even hosts active volcanoes.

phys-org.title: Mapping project helps protect coastal world heritage sites from climate threats
phys-org.description: A major new digital mapping project could help safeguard some of the world's most important and well-known heritage sites from rising seas, flooding and coastal erosion. Researchers led by scientists from the University of East Anglia (UEA), Durham University and the University of Cape Town have created the Global Coastal Heritage (Glo-CoH) dataset, the first comprehensive digital map of UNESCO World Heritage sites located along coastlines less than 20 meters (66 feet) above sea level.

phys-org.title: Thousands flee wildfires in southern Europe

phys-org.title: 3D-printed bioplastic pods offer new hope for seagrass restoration in Thailand
phys-org.description: A new collaborative research project between Murdoch University and Walailak University (WU) aims to restore seagrass meadows in Thailand using 3D-printed pods made from bioplastics.

phys-org.title: Researchers explore classroom applications of AI new learning platforms

phys-org.title: How an iceberg may have stopped emperor penguins from breeding on Coulman Island in 2025
phys-org.description: The number of chicks in the Coulman Island emperor penguin colony decreased by about 69% in 2025 compared with 2024, according to research published in Communications Earth & Environment. The authors suggest that a large iceberg, which grounded off the island between July 2025 and January 2026, likely restricted the colony's access to important foraging areas, demonstrating that individual iceberg movements may affect breeding success even when overall sea ice conditions appear favorable.

The new framework will apply after a two-year transition period. It distinguishes between two categories. Although these mirror-image forms may look almost identical, they can behave very differently in chemical reactions, biological systems and advanced materials. Preparing one mirror-image form in high purity is therefore an important goal in chemistry.

phys-org.title: How researchers are using AI to speed up drug discovery and development: Q&A
phys-org.description: Drug development is among the slowest, most failure-prone processes in modern science, with about 90% of drug candidates never reaching the market. Today, artificial intelligence methods have accelerated the first step—plucking promising molecules out of endless possibilities—but countless challenges remain. A successful drug must be not only safe and effective but also able to bypass the body's defenses and reach the right target.

At regular intervals, they descend to a depth of 2,000 meters (6,600 feet) and, as they rise, measure parameters such as temperature, salinity and pressure. phys-org.title: Alan Turing's gay short story reveals 'fun, cheeky' man who loved sex and literature
phys-org.description: A startling new study of a little-known, unpublished short story by Alan Turing challenges our understanding of the man who played a key role in cracking the Nazis' Enigma code, developed the theoretical underpinnings of the first computers and laid the groundwork for the development of artificial intelligence.

phys-org.title: Could alien signals be hiding on a different radio channel?
phys-org.description: Astronomers searching for signs of extraterrestrial intelligence may have been missing alien signals in part of the radio spectrum that has not recently been explored.

phys-org.title: When mothers make the winners: How alpha female lineages dominate hyena clans
phys-org.description: In mammals, males are usually stronger and more competitive than females. Males also show greater inequality in reproductive success—the number of offspring they produce—than females. In spotted hyenas, the opposite is true: Reproductive inequality is greater among females than males. The reason? Female spotted hyenas pass on their social rank and the associated privileges, such as priority access to food, to their offspring, whereas males do not.

Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

proj-syn.title: What Ukraine’s Success Means for the West
proj-syn.description: There are several reasons why Ukraine has been able to stymie its much larger aggressor. For the world’s democracies, the most important lesson to draw from Ukrainians' doggedness and brilliant innovations and improvisations may be that we should not be so surprised.

proj-syn.title: The Strong Suffer What They Must
proj-syn.description: Foolish military interventions driven by outdated calculations of economic power have thoroughly discredited the old big powers. Thucydides might well have appreciated the irony of a world in which smaller, weaker countries like Ukraine and Iran can expose Russia and the United States, respectively, as paper tigers.

proj-syn.title: Yes, the Hong Kong of Old Is Over
proj-syn.description: The pro-China camp continues to tout Hong Kong’s resilience, recently pointing to the fact that the city has reclaimed its position as the global IPO leader. But conveniently left out of this narrative is that resilience has come to depend on the direct intervention of the Chinese authorities.

proj-syn.title: Why Iran Won’t Change
proj-syn.description: Embedded in the Islamic Republic’s foundations is a doctrine that allows for total repression of the population and mobilization of all state resources to preserve the system. This helps to explain why the US and Israel were wrong to expect the regime to change its behavior, let alone be brought down by the Iranian people.

proj-syn.title: Rethinking Global Imbalances
proj-syn.description: Today’s global imbalances, starting with China's massive trade surplus, are not simply the result of poor macroeconomic coordination. Rather, they reflect long-term strategic thinking and a departure from the bias toward openness on which the postwar trade order was built.

proj-syn.title: What the New UK Chancellor Means for the UK Economy
proj-syn.description: By appointing John Healey as chancellor of the exchequer, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has taken a calculated risk. If Healey can leverage his insider knowledge of the Treasury, pursue a bold, pro-growth agenda, and manage his defense-spending instincts, he may be able to provide the structural shake-up the UK economy needs.

proj-syn.title: Will the US Climate War with Canada Become Global?
proj-syn.description: For the first time, a great power has moved to price transboundary climate-driven harms–massive wildfires–and extract compensation unilaterally. What was previously a development, insurance, or emissions-accounting issue is now a security and trade dispute between two G7 economies, setting a precedent that others may try to follow.

proj-syn.title: America Is Closing the Door on Opportunity—and Talent
proj-syn.description: Viewed in isolation, the Trump administration's new, more restrictive student-visa policy may seem modest. But as part of a broader retreat from openness, it signals that the country once known for offering ambitious outsiders a chance to transform their lives is less willing to do so.

proj-syn.title: Large Language Models for Small Language Communities
proj-syn.description: Many developing economies cannot access large language models, most of which have been trained on datasets in English. To build scalable and inclusive LLMs for countries with minority languages, policymakers' best bet is to tap mobile network operators, with their armies of developers and data-processing capabilities.

proj-syn.title: The Epstein Class Was Made Offshore
proj-syn.description: The impunity of Jeffrey Epstein and his associates is the predictable upshot of unbridled wealth concentration, facilitated by the offshore financial system. In fact, that system represents the selective withdrawal by a privileged few from the rule of law, without the loss of any of its benefits.

proj-syn.title: A New Tool for Combating Human Trafficking
proj-syn.description: While human trafficking is mostly framed as a macro phenomenon, this does not fully explain how these criminal networks operate. Recognizing that trafficking corridors link specific source and destination localities offers a stronger basis for policy than a purely national approach or isolated interventions.

proj-syn.title: The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly in Global Tax Negotiations
proj-syn.description: Ongoing negotiations at the United Nations offer the international community the best chance that it will have to ensure that global taxation authority is assigned fairly. With multinationals and the ultra-rich abusing the current system to minimize their tax payments, finalizing a new convention is an urgent priority.

proj-syn.title: The Bayer Truth About Trump’s Farm and Food Policies
proj-syn.description: A new executive order on regenerative agriculture might seem to suggest that US President Donald Trump’s administration wants to help American farmers. But a closer look at the order and other recent developments reveals a familiar pattern: an unhappy public gets reassuring words, while corporate interests receive tangible support.

proj-syn.title: Don’t Overestimate America and China’s Importance
proj-syn.description: Some commentators on international affairs seem to think that “the West” and the BRICS+ do not really matter; only the United States and China do. Yet three factors complicate this simplistic framing, suggesting that even superpowers' influence has limits, and that smaller powers can sometimes punch above their weight.

proj-syn.title: Colombia’s Rightward Turn
proj-syn.description: There is a growing tension in Colombia between the popular demand for a strong welfare state and a political system that cannot deliver on that promise unless it breaks free from malign influences. Since the incoming administration is aligned with many of those interests, Colombians will continue to be disappointed.

proj-syn.title: A Cold War Adventure in Portugal
proj-syn.description: Just 52 years after escaping military dictatorship, Portugal is an EU and eurozone member and the world’s seventh-safest country. While Donald Trump's systematic destruction of the rules-based global order will not reverse this progress, nor will it do any good for Portugal, the US, or anyone else.

proj-syn.title: Social-Media Age Bans Won’t Make Children Safer—But This Will
proj-syn.description: As the European Union considers how to protect and empower young people in a digital world, it must resist the urge only to enact a ban on social media for young people. A more effective strategy would force tech companies to remove addictive features by holding them to product-liability standards—as with most other industries.
